newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds see Belgium hold at 9 bp,more rand deals.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds see Belgium hold at 9 bp,more rand deals.

text.p: ** The primary market on Tuesday was dominated by Belgium's
$500 million 5-year Euro-Asian bond amid still more rand deals.
** Belgium priced its $500 million five-year bond to yield nine
basis points over U.S. Treasury notes and said it could
launch up to three more Eurobond issues this year.
** The success of recent zero-coupon rand deals saw the
World Bank launch another 2.0 bln rand 25-year bond as well
as a 200 million rand one-year bond with a 16.0 pct coupon.
** There was also activity in the lire sector.
"The market is short of sovereign paper," the UBS source said.
Belgium is rated AA1 by Moody's Investors Service and AA+ by Standard & Poor's Corp.
Dealers said selling had resumed in the Eurobond market, with 10-year dollar particularly hit. Spread widened by up to two notches. Some investors switched out of 10-year bonds into Belgium's paper.
An official at joint lead manager Morgan Stanley said there had been strong demand from non-Japan Asia and Swiss and Benelux investors.
But many investors were still on the sidelines as they awaited further U.S. data.

On Wednesday, the Federal Reserve releases its Beige Book of economic activity which will be closely analysed to see whether U.S. rates are likely to rise at the March 25 Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
Retail sales figures due Thursday and producer price data scheduled for release of Friday will also be closely watched.
Meanwhile, Russian officials met investors in Zurich in preparation for a debut mark Eurobond, its second international debt issue.
The deal could be for up to two billion marks and is expected to have a seven-year maturity.
But it was still too early for firm details regarding the exact timing and pricing of the deal, traders said.

"Everyone is waiting for Wednesday's presentation in Frankfurt, which is more important, and after that there may be a clearer indication of what is expected," a banker familiar with the transaction said.
The World Bank reflected its bullishness on the South African rand with two more deals following the success of its other recent issues.

Syndicate officials say the high yields, certain tax advantages, small cash outlay to buy the paper as well as hopes of long-term rand appreciation and expectations of a fall in interest rates were the driving force behind the rand issuance.
South African Finance Minister Trevor Manuel will present his maiden budget for 1997/98 on Wednesday.
-- Hayley Pienaar, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7718
